title: Base change preserves pinned split realizations and their based data
statement: Let $A\to C$ be a unital homomorphism between nonzero commutative rings and let $P=(G,T,M,\Phi,\Phi^\vee,\Delta,(X_\alpha))$ be a pinned split realization over $A$ of a finite reduced based root datum $\mathcal R$ [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization]. Pullback of the group scheme, torus, characters, cocharacters and named simple-root tangent vectors along $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-fibre-product] gives a pinned split realization $P_C$ over $C$ of the same abstract based datum $\mathcal R$. Under the canonical tangent comparison, its root spaces are $C\otimes_A\mathfrak g_\alpha$ and its pinning generators are $1\otimes X_\alpha$. This conclusion holds for arbitrary $A\to C$, including nonflat maps, and respects successive base changes and base change of pinning-compatible isomorphisms.

proof.text: Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $S_C=\operatorname{Spec}C$ and $G_C=G\times_S S_C$, $T_C=T\times_S S_C$. Pull back multiplication, identity and inverse by the fibre-product universal property. Each group identity remains an equality: its two sides have identical projections to $G$ and $S_C$, so uniqueness in that universal property equates them. The same argument pulls back the inclusion and any group homomorphism, and preserves composition and inverses.

source.place: Section 3.1, definition of reductive group schemes; elementary pullback of the group diagrams.

proof.text: The base-changed $G_C\to S_C$ is smooth by clause (2) of [lem-pc-proper-base-change], affine by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], and of finite presentation by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. The base change of the closed immersion $T\to G$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. These statements allow an arbitrary base morphism.

A geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S_C$ is also a geometric point of $S$ by composition. The universal property identifies $(G_C)_\Omega$ with $G_\Omega$ and $(T_C)_\Omega$ with $T_\Omega$, compatibly with inclusion and all group maps: both iterated products classify the same pairs of maps. Thus connectedness, reductivity, maximality of the torus, and the prescribed geometric root--coroot correspondence hold on this fibre because they hold for $P$ at that same geometric point of $S$. This uses every geometric point in the given definition, not only one chosen algebraic closure per point.

source.place: Section 3.1, printed p.81, Definition 3.1.1; Definition 5.1.1, printed p.136: check the given fibrewise conditions on the identical geometric fibre.

proof.text: The affine fibre-product formula gives $T_C=\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_A A[M])$. The maps $c\otimes\sum_m a_m e_m\mapsto\sum_m c f(a_m)e_m$ and $\sum_m c_m e_m\mapsto\sum_m c_m\otimes e_m$ are inverse algebra maps to $C[M]$ by the finite-basis expansion and the tensor relations. They preserve coproduct, counit and antipode on each $e_m$. Consequently $T_C=D_C(M)$. A character $m$ and a cocharacter $y\in M^\vee$ retain the maps $t\mapsto e_m$ on character coordinates and $e_m\mapsto t^{\langle m,y\rangle}$ on cocharacter coordinates. The integer pairing, roots, coroots and the chosen base in the abstract lattice are unchanged.

source.place: Appendix B.1, printed p.280, group algebra construction; Definition 5.1.1, printed p.136. Explicit basis calculation.

proof.text: Write $G=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $u:B\to A$ for its identity. The smooth-affine criterion makes $B$ a smooth $A$-algebra. A tangent point is exactly $b\mapsto u(b)+\epsilon d(b)$; comparing products modulo $\epsilon^2$ gives $d(bb')=u(b)d(b')+u(b')d(b)$. Hence $\mathfrak g=T(B,u)$. This identification respects its module structure: if $\mu^*b=\sum_i b_i\otimes b_i'$, multiplication of tangent points has coefficient $\sum_i d(b_i)u(b_i')+u(b_i)d'(b_i')=d(b)+d'(b)$ by the two unit identities, and $\epsilon\mapsto a\epsilon$ gives $ad$. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-augmented-tangent-scalar-extension] to obtain $\theta_C:C\otimes_A\mathfrak g\simeq\operatorname{Lie}(G_C)$, with coefficient formula $c\otimes d$ acting on $c'\otimes b$ as $cc'f(d(b))$. The affine fibre-product formula identifies its coordinate algebra with $C\otimes_A B$.

source.place: Tags 00RO, 00RV and 00T2; affine smoothness comparison in more-morphisms.tex, Tag 02H6. Dual-number and multiplication coefficient calculations written out.

proof.text: Let $\rho:\mathfrak g\to A[M]\otimes_A\mathfrak g$ be the given coaction of $T=D_A(M)$: conjugation by the universal point $t_A\in T(A[M])$, whose coordinate map is the identity of $A[M]$ [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group], is an $A[M]$-algebra automorphism $\kappa_A$ of $B_{A[M]}=A[M]\otimes_AB$ fixing the identity augmentation, and $\rho$ is precomposition with $\kappa_A$ read through $\theta_{A[M]}$. By step 2 for the base changes along $A\to A[M]$ and $A\to C[M]$, with [lem-pc-proper-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] on the affine fibre products [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $B_{A[M]}$ is smooth over $A[M]$ and $B_C$ over $C$, so the new lemma applies to them. The universal point $t_C\in T_C(C[M])$ is the image of $t_A$ under $A[M]\to C[M]$, $ae_m\mapsto f(a)e_m$, since both send $e_m\mapsto e_m$; hence the conjugation automorphism $\kappa_C$ of $C[M]\otimes_AB=C[M]\otimes_{A[M]}B_{A[M]}$ is $C[M]\otimes_{A[M]}\kappa_A$. Naturality in [lem-sfb-smooth-augmented-tangent-scalar-extension] over the base $A[M]$, with $q=\kappa_A$ and coefficient ring $C[M]$, says precomposition with $\kappa_C$ is $C[M]\otimes_{A[M]}$ of precomposition with $\kappa_A$. Its tower compatibility for $A\to A[M]\to C[M]$ and for $A\to C\to C[M]$ identifies both sides with $C[M]\otimes_A\mathfrak g$ compatibly with $\theta_C$. As $t_C$ has the identity of $C[M]$ as coordinate map, equality at this point is equality of coaction maps: the coaction of $T_C$ on $\operatorname{Lie}(G_C)\cong C\otimes_A\mathfrak g$ is $C\otimes\rho$. Every $t\in T_C(R)$ is a specialization of $t_C$, so this is the full scheme-theoretic action, not its restriction to residue-field points.

source.place: Section 4 opening, printed p.107: Lie algebra as an M-graded vector bundle; tangent naturality applied at the universal torus point.

proof.text: Tensor the given finite decomposition $\mathfrak g=\operatorname{Lie}(T)\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi}\mathfrak g_\alpha$ by $C$. Its summand inclusions $j_m$ and projections $p_m$ still satisfy $p_mj_n=\delta_{mn}$ and $\sum_mj_mp_m=1$ after tensoring, so it remains a direct decomposition without flatness. In the coaction of step 6 each summand has its original monomial $e_m$. If $w=\sum_mw_m$ has weight $\alpha$, comparing coefficients in the free basis $(e_m)$ of $C[M]$ gives $w_m=0$ for $m\ne\alpha$, hence the root space is exactly $C\otimes_A\mathfrak g_\alpha$. Coefficient comparison is valid for every module $V$: the maps $v\otimes\sum c_me_m\mapsto(c_mv)_m$ and $(v_m)_m\mapsto\sum v_m\otimes e_m$ are inverse on finitely supported families. For the torus itself a tangent point has $e_m\mapsto1+\epsilon z(m)$, with $z:M\to A$ additive, since $e_me_n=e_{m+n}$. A finite lattice basis identifies these maps with $A^r$, and after base change with $C^r$, by the same coefficient formula. The formula for $\theta_C$ commutes with the inclusion $T\to G$ on dual-number points, so the zero summand is exactly $\operatorname{Lie}(T_C)$.

source.place: Section 4 opening, printed p.107 and Theorem 3.3.4 proof, p.99: weight decomposition under base change. Split-projection and coefficient argument supplied here.

proof.text: For each root choose the given rank-one trivialization $A\simeq\mathfrak g_\alpha$. Tensoring its inverse and forward maps yields inverse maps $C\simeq C\otimes_A\mathfrak g_\alpha$, since $c\otimes a\mapsto cf(a)$ identifies $C\otimes_A A$ with $C$. For a simple root use the specified map $a\mapsto aX_\alpha$; its tensor is $c\mapsto c(1\otimes X_\alpha)$. Thus every root space is free of rank one and every named simple-root vector is a generator. Together with steps 1--7 these are exactly all the conditions for a pinned split realization of the unchanged based datum.

source.place: Definitions 5.1.1 and 6.1.1, printed pp.136 and 186; tensor the specified trivializations and their inverses.

proof.text: For $A\to C\xrightarrow h D$, successive scheme pullbacks have the same projections and are uniquely isomorphic by the fibre-product property. On group-algebra coordinates the identification sends $d\otimes(c\otimes e_m)$ to $dh(c)\otimes e_m$. The tangent lemma gives the same formula on $d\otimes(c\otimes v)$, including each root summand, so both constructions send the pinning to $1\otimes X_\alpha$. Finally, for a pinning-compatible isomorphism $F:P\simeq P'$, its pullback is an isomorphism by step 1, its torus map is the same lattice map on monomials, and tangent naturality gives $dF_C(1\otimes X_\alpha)=1\otimes dF(X_\alpha)=1\otimes X'_{\sigma(\alpha)}$. These equations prove the asserted compatibility on morphisms as well as on objects, with identity and composition inherited from pullback.
